clue.text: Not even Blair mistook Noel for singer

indicators.note: not the even letters, so only the odd-numbered letters of the run of words are kept

explanation.surface: A former prime minister misidentifies a Noel and takes him for a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not even' looks like an intensifier ('not even Blair could...') but tells you to drop the even letters of BLAIRMISTOOKNOEL, leaving the odd ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice type between tenor and bass names the man who sings in that range.

clue.text: Good exercise channel

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good in crossword usage
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A television station devoted to fitness that is actually worth watching.
explanation.definitionFit: A tube carrying water or gas is a conduit, a kind of channel.

clue.text: Sat about with relative inactivity

indicators.note: about can mean round and about, so the letters of sat are moved around

parts.note: sis, short for sister, is a relative

explanation.surface: Someone lounged around doing nothing in the company of a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the anagram signal here, not 'concerning'; 'relative inactivity' reads as one phrase but splits after 'relative'.
explanation.definitionFit: Equilibrium in which nothing changes is a state of inactivity or stagnation.

clue.text: Lock trouble revealed by open door?

definitions.text: Lock trouble revealed by open door?

parts.words: Lock trouble revealed by open door?
parts.note: a lock here is a lock of hair, and its trouble is a frayed tip; the second reading turns open into split and door into the end of a house

explanation.surface: A locksmith's problem discovered when a door is found ajar.
explanation.walkthrough: The lock is hair, not a door fitting; a damaged tip on a hair is the trouble. 'Open' suggests split and a door is at an end of a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Frayed tips on strands of hair are a common hairdressing complaint about locks.

clue.text: Heavenly image could upset Catholic primate after Sunday

indicators.note: after places the Catholic primate following the abbreviation for Sunday
upset means knocked over, so the letters of could are rearranged

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A picture of heaven might offend a senior Catholic bishop when shown after Sunday mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catholic primate' reads as an archbishop but is C plus APE.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting or view of the sky full of clouds is an image of the heavens.

clue.text: Pop icon collects casual shirt as formal wear

indicators.note: collects means takes in, so the pop icon holds the shirt inside

parts.note: David Bowie was a pop icon
a T-shirt is a casual shirt, shortened to T

explanation.surface: A rock star gathers a T-shirt and wears it as evening dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A neckwear knot worn with dinner jackets is part of formal evening dress.

clue.text: Heater or cooler?

definitions.meaning: a household device for warming rooms, fed by hot water
in a car engine, the device that keeps it from overheating

explanation.surface: A question about whether an appliance warms or chills.
explanation.definitionFit: The domestic panel warms a room while the car part cools an engine, so one word covers both.

clue.text: Start to record first bees on tape

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, means first
two Bs spoken are bees

explanation.surface: Instructions for taping a recording of bees.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow strip of fabric or ink tape is a band, a strip like tape.

clue.text: "Close to drop, Villa lack wingers!" — cry of suffering supporter

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter
a word lacking its wings keeps only its middle letters

parts.note: ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: An Aston Villa fan groans that the team, short of wide players, is near relegation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' looks like the football fan but is the thing a head rests on. Aston Villa is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushion for the head supports it in bed.

clue.text: Irishman delivered flower

indicators.note: delivered as a speech, so the name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Neil is an Irish man's name

explanation.surface: An Irish man brought a bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is something that flows: a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is something that flows, so crosswords call it a flower; this is the African river.

clue.text: Criminal robs quite special handles

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: A villain steals some rather distinctive door handles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handles' looks like door fittings but is slang for names.
explanation.definitionFit: Handle is slang for a name, and nicknames are names given informally.

clue.text: With 40% cash, Dave's other half gets the drinks

indicators.note: forty per cent of a five-letter word is its first two letters

parts.note: cash means money
Chas and Dave were a British singing duo, so Chas is Dave's partner

explanation.surface: A man spends part of his cash on a round for himself and his partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Chas & Dave were a cockney pop duo from London.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffees flavoured with chocolate are popular café drinks.

clue.text: Critical journalist's article on fixing the match

indicators.note: on means added to, so the article follows
fixing a match means rigging it, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A reporter writes a piece exposing a rigged football game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixing' rearranges THE MATCH into HATCHETM.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer hired to savage reputations is a ruthless critic, a hired attacker in print.

clue.text: Olive Oyl forgets Popeye's 5th anniversary

indicators.note: forgets means leaves out a letter from the name
fifth letter of the sailor's name, counting from the start

parts.note: Easter is the yearly commemoration of the Resurrection

explanation.surface: Popeye forgets his wedding anniversary with his cartoon girlfriend Olive Oyl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olive' looks like part of the cartoon name but is the definition; Y, the fifth letter of POPEYE, leaves OYL.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild olive tree of the Mediterranean is a kind of olive.

clue.text: Afraid to grip the wedge?

indicators.note: to grip means to hold within, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: afraid is in fear

explanation.surface: A nervous golfer can't hold the wedge club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wedge' looks like a golf club; it is a tapered strip.
explanation.definitionFit: In carpentry a tapered key or tongue fitted into a groove is a slip of wood shaped like a wedge.

clue.text: Preserved them clipped, without hair, without tips of moustache

indicators.note: clipped means cut short, as in the informal shortened form of the pronoun
without means outside, so the hairless word goes round the tips

parts.note: having no hair is bald

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A barber cuts some people's hair off and trims their moustache ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'without's do different jobs: the first means lacking, the second means outside. 'Them clipped' is the informal 'em.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodies treated with spices and chemicals are preserved from decay, as in mummification.

clue.text: Increase loan

definitions.meaning: a rise or step forward, as in prices going up
money handed over early, as against future salary

explanation.definitionFit: A forward step is a rise, and money handed over before it is due is a loan.

clue.text: Monk might be in church, albeit tormented

indicators.note: in places the anagram inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: tormented means twisted in pain, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monk in church who is nonetheless troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monk might be' is a definition by example: chastity is what a monk vows.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks take vows of chastity, so a monk is expected to be unmarried and chaste.

clue.text: Series: The Saint, complete with halo

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
a halo is a ring of light

explanation.surface: A television series called The Saint, its hero shown with a halo.
explanation.walkthrough: The Saint was a British TV series whose hero's emblem was a stick figure with a halo.
explanation.definitionFit: A succession of related things, like a string of wins, is a series.

clue.text: A mobile device promoting line for letters

indicators.note: promoting means moving up, so the line goes to the front

parts.note: a phablet is a large mobile phone, part phone part tablet

explanation.surface: An advert for a phone that is being promoted by a product line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoting' looks like advertising but means moving the line letter up to the front of the device's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The full set of letters of a writing system, A to Z.

clue.text: Coward uplifted by 1 down's shooting star

indicators.note: by means next to, so the reference follows
uplifted means raised, in a down entry read from the bottom up

parts.note: Noel Coward was a playwright
1 down is written 1D in crossword references, and 1 looks like I

explanation.surface: A cowardly singer is lifted up by the singer of another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' is Noel Coward, the English playwright, not a timid person.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor from the November Leonid shower, which seems to come from Leo, is a shooting star.

clue.text: The girl Lois empties guts when fed 50 crusts

parts.note: she is a girl referred to

indicators.note: fed means given something to take inside
taking out the guts leaves only the outside letters

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: Lois, a girl cooking, guts a fish and feeds fifty people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empties guts' reduces LOIS to LS, which takes L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard outer cases, such as of nuts or eggs, are crusts or husks.

clue.text: Twist succeeded — April fool!

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

indicators.note: fool means to mess about, so the letters are played around with

explanation.surface: An April Fool prank came off, with a twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A coil or helix is a twisting curve.

clue.text: Food cooked in little cases (yellow)

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so the anagram goes round the colour
cooked means doctored, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: Pasta cooked in small yellow parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: The heraldic colour for yellow or gold is or; 'cases' means the anagram wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring-shaped stuffed pasta is a food.

clue.text: Rotavate earth, except underground

indicators.note: to rotavate is to turn the soil with a rotating machine, so here the word is turned round

parts.note: but means except

explanation.surface: Instructions for tilling the soil, apart from the subsoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotavate' means turn, so E plus BUT is turned round as one piece. The Tube is the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tube is the informal name for the London Underground railway.

clue.text: Double 2 minus 0 plus 1 number

indicators.note: minus means take away, so the zero is removed from the word

parts.note: the figure 2 is the word two
zero looks like O
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sum: two doubled, less nothing, plus one.
explanation.definitionFit: An identical counterpart or lookalike is a double.

clue.text: IT are furious about the source of DOS attack

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the anagram goes round the letter
furious means wild, so the letters are mixed up
the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The IT department are angry about the cause of a denial-of-service attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furious' turns IT ARE into TIRAE, which holds D.
explanation.definitionFit: A long angry speech is a verbal attack.

clue.text: Freeze injured cartilage right away

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the letters are rearranged
away means taken off, so the letter for right is removed from the pool

explanation.surface: Ice an injured knee cartilage straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like immediately; it means remove R before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover with ice or glaciers is to freeze over.
